sections.h2: Fastest route to selling in Yonkers
sections.html:
Owners can hire a broker, sell privately, or deal with a cash buyer who takes the house in its present condition. One cost to plan for is a city transfer tax of 1.5 percent of the price, charged to the seller above the state's own tax.

Yonkers lies in Westchester County just north of the Bronx, and it had 212,603 residents in the July 1, 2025 estimate, the most of any city in the county. Delays usually trace to three items: the city's property files, the tax installments, and a transfer tax return that must be stamped before the deed is recorded.

Owners are the minority here, so apartment buildings and small multifamily houses make up a large share of what trades.

Whoever buys a house with tenants will want the leases and rent records, so assemble them before showing the property.

sections.h2: Layout of the city and its quarters
sections.html:
The city has about 18 square miles of dry land. The Hudson River forms its western edge, the Bronx River separates it from Mount Vernon, Tuckahoe, Bronxville and Scarsdale on the east, and the Bronx begins at its southern line. The Saw Mill River splits the city into four quarters and meets the Hudson at Getty Square, the downtown and civic center.

  • Northeast: Crestwood, Colonial Heights, Cedar Knolls and Lawrence Park West, close to several Metro-North stations.
  • Northwest: Nepera Park, Runyon Heights, Homefield, Glenwood and Greystone, with Victorian houses and views of the Palisades.
  • Southeast: Dunwoodie and the McLean Avenue area, where buildings recall the Bronx and Queens.
  • Southwest: Getty Square, Park Hill, Nodine Hill, Lowerre and Hudson Park, a blend of apartments, row houses and detached homes.

Rail is a big draw. Hudson Line trains stop at Ludlow, Yonkers, Glenwood and Greystone on the way to Manhattan, Amtrak's Empire Service calls at the Yonkers station, and Harlem Line stops lie along the eastern boundary. Highway links include I-87 and the Saw Mill, Bronx River, Sprain Brook and Cross County parkways.

Flash flooding in September 2023 brought a local state of emergency, and crews pumped water from homes afterward. A basement that took water will draw questions from the buyer's inspector and insurer, so keep repair receipts.

The Department of Housing and Buildings grants building permits and certificates of occupancy, inspects work and looks into complaints. Applications are filed online through City Squared.

  • A permit to renovate an existing dwelling for one to three families requires a Home Improvement Contractor's License, which the Consumer Protection Bureau issues.
  • Property files are reviewed by appointment, so have the block and lot at hand. The department is digitizing paper records and emails a link in place of an office visit.
  • The link may arrive after the appointment date, which is a reason to ask early.

Older Yonkers houses commonly have additions and finished basements, and the file is where a buyer's attorney checks for matching permits.

Homeowners receive two bills. The county bill comes in March and is paid in a single payment, due in April. The City and School bill comes in July and is divided into three equal installments.

  • First installment: late July, 30 days after the city sets its budget.
  • Second: October 6, shifted off a weekend if needed.
  • Third: January 6, shifted off a weekend if needed. The next one is Wednesday, January 6, 2027.

Yonkers offers no grace period. Late installments earn 15 percent annual interest, figured daily from the confirmation date, and the city says it cannot forgive that interest. The envelope postmark decides whether a mailed payment was on time.

Title and mortgage companies may research parcels free online or order a Tax Office search at $5 per property per year, with a two to three week lead time. Payments go to City Hall, Room 108, at 40 South Broadway.

sections.h2: What to have ready before an offer
sections.html:
A Yonkers sale runs smoothly when the folder is complete. Pull the property file from the Department of Housing and Buildings by appointment, with the block and lot ready, and look for permits that match any additions or finished basements. Print the current county and City and School bills so the buyer's attorney can see which installments are paid.

If tenants live in the house, add the leases and rent records. If the basement ever took water, add the repair receipts. With those in hand, the attorney can file the city transfer tax return the moment the deed is delivered and stay inside the seven-day window.

A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal and takes the house in its current condition, which spares you repairs and the wait for a bank. The city and state transfer taxes, the tax installments and the county recording still apply, so the stamped receipt and the deed paperwork are the items to line up. If timing is tight, ask your attorney to prepare the return in advance, since the city says email is the quickest way to get the stamp.

The Assessment Department keeps a fixed calendar, and the filing period lasts only two weeks.

  • October 15: taxable status date, and the last day to file or renew senior, disability and military service exemptions.
  • November 1: tentative roll published.
  • November 1 to 15: complaints go to the Board of Assessment Review.
  • December 15: cutoff for added information or a personal hearing request.
  • Last Monday in January to the third Friday in February: hearings.
  • April 10: final roll. Owners who protested can seek Small Claims Assessment Review through the county from April 10 to May 10.

The period closes on November 15 every year, and anyone who misses it waits twelve months.

The city tax is 1.5 percent of the selling price and falls on the seller. Sales of $25,000 or less owe nothing, and co-op units are exempt. The payment is due within seven days after the deed is handed over and before it is recorded. Seller and buyer each file a return, even if no tax is owed.

The order of steps: file the return, pay, collect the stamped receipt, then bring that receipt to the Westchester County Clerk when the deed is recorded. The city says email is quickest for getting the stamp, and mailed copies go to City Hall, Room 108.

The state adds its own base tax, and Form TP-584 goes to the county clerk within 15 days of delivery. The buyer owes a 1 percent mansion tax once a residence reaches $1 million.

faqs.q: What does Yonkers transfer tax cost?
faqs.a: The city charges 1.5 percent of the price. The seller pays the city within seven days after the deed is delivered and before it is recorded.

faqs.q: When is the next Yonkers City tax installment due?
faqs.a: Wednesday, January 6, 2027, for the third installment of the 2026/27 bill. Installments fall in late July, on October 6 and on January 6 each year.

faqs.q: Does Yonkers add interest if a payment is a day late?
faqs.a: Yes. With no grace period, interest of 15 percent a year accrues from the confirmation date, figured daily, and the city says it cannot be waived.

faqs.q: How do I see the building file for my Yonkers house?
faqs.a: Book an appointment with the Department of Housing and Buildings and supply the block and lot. The department then emails a link to its paper and digital records.

faqs.q: Which office records a Yonkers deed?
faqs.a: The Westchester County Clerk does. Yonkers stamps its own transfer tax receipt first, and that receipt goes to the clerk along with the deed.
